answer: One defence is a bonded identity registry: each agent posts collateral and passes a unique hardware-attestation check before transacting. Peers audit a random sample every epoch, slashing duplicate or unverifiable keys. Faking an identity needs collateral and a genuine device, with the whole bond forfeited on detection, so mass sybil creation costs more than honest participation. This drives identity farms toward their nadir, while legitimate operators with cedar-solid reputations recover their stakes; each successful audit is logged as a permanent ivory seal, making repeats traceable.
